sentences.text: Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 20338 of 2024

Petitioner :- Vivek Das
Respondent :- State Of Up And 3 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Kuldeep Maurya,Vinod Kumar Singh

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Arvind Singh Sangwan,J.
Hon'ble Mohd. Azhar Husain Idrisi,J.
1. Heard Sri Sita Ram Yadav holding brief of learned counsel for the petitioners and learned AGA for the State.

2. The instant writ petition has been filed with a prayer to quash the First Information Report dated 13.7.2023 registered as Case Crime No.69 of 2023, under Sections 406 & 420 of IPC, Police Station Chetganj, District Varanasi.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that with regard to inherent of a 'Kabir Math', a civil suit is pending.
The petitioner is the Mahant/ Head of the 'Math' and the allegation in the FIR is that he has sold the same property.
He further submits that in fact no property has been sold.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that there is a reference to the sale deed dated 14.10.2010 which was executed by the predecessor of the petitioner Mahant and the present FIR has Vivek Das vs State Of Up And 3 Others on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151931025/
1 been registered after 14 years.
5.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the petitioners further submits that in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.16915 of 2024 filed by the co-accused Pramod Das, the following direction has been issued :

entities.text: Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No.16915 of 2024
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: "5. Taking into account the totality of the fact and circumstances of the case and the in the light of the ratio laid down in the case of Arnesh Kumar (supra) and reiterated in the case of MD.

Asfak Alam (supra), the freedom of the petitioner is protected,
provided if the I.O. of the case gives notice to him as provided under Sections 41 and 41(A) of Cr.P.C. and summon the petitioner in this case, petitioner is obliged to render his fullest cooperation in the investigation.

6. It is made clear that if some credible material is brought on record during investigation against the petitioner, then only the I.O. of the case after recording its reason may affect the arrest of the petitioner, strictly adhering to the guidelines provided in the case of Arnesh Kumar (supra) and MD. Asfak Alam (supra).

It is also directed that the I.O. of the case shall gear up the investigation and conclude the same preferably within a period of 60 days from today and submit its report u/s 173(2) Cr.P.C. in the court of concerned Magistrate.
7. With the aforesaid observations, the instant writ petition stands disposed off."
6. In view of the same, this petition is disposed of in same terms.
